Working notes:
- Handled REQ-2400–REQ-2409: all were large requests “originating from the east region” needing assignment to the right desk.
- Request types seen: shipment, invoice, refund. Senders/desks varied; no pattern proved decisive.
- Options seen: A (standard queue), B (priority desk), C (regional office/regional).
- Action tried on every ticket: C. Outcome: rejected each time (+0.00), with reason “option C is not valid for this request.”
- Therefore: do not choose C for this class of east-region large requests. Urgency phrases (“asking twice,” “second attempt,” “first form bounced,” “scanned, not typed,” “came through regional office”) did not make C valid.
- No outcome yet for A or B. Next similar ticket: choose between A and B, then record result to establish correct desk.
- Useful context: subject/request type and sender vary, but the core task remains assignment of east-region large shipment/invoice/refund requests.

Working notes:

- C is not valid for this class. Do not choose C.
- Correct desk is determined by request type, not sender or urgency wording.
- Shipment: choose B. REQ-2413, REQ-2415, REQ-2418 accepted with B. A was rejected for shipment on REQ-2410.
- Refund: choose A. REQ-2416 accepted with A. B was rejected for refund on REQ-2412, REQ-2417, REQ-2419.
- Claim: B was rejected on REQ-2411 and REQ-2414. C is invalid. If D is offered, choose D; if only A/B/C, A is the likely remaining valid option and should be tested.
- Invoice: no new outcome recorded; still unresolved. Do not assume A or B until tested.
- Urgency/sender phrases did not determine validity: “asking twice,” “second attempt,” “first form bounced,” “scanned, not typed,” “came through regional office,” “same as last month,” “no rush,” “confirm receipt.”
- Next similar ticket: classify by request type. Shipment -> B; refund -> A; claim -> D if available, otherwise test A; invoice -> test A/B and record.
